sourceRefs.excerpt: TM Wealth Enhancer is a whole life single premium investment-linked plan that allows you to invest in a range of investment-linked funds while providing protection against death as long as the policy is in force. The pre

notes: Models the published 100% allocation of the initial CPF-funded single premium with no additional premium charge.

catalogWarnings: TM Wealth Enhancer (CPFIS) is cataloged as a supported V1 product. The parser captures the published zero-charge single-premium, ad-hoc top-up, regular top-up, and nil-charge withdrawal path for the CPF-funded corridor through the open-ended no-MIP basis, plus the current ordinary death-benefit estimate as 105% of the single premium policy value and 100% of the top-up premium policy value, while split policy-value history, fund-level charges, switching administration, and lapse / termination handling remain informational only.

TM Wealth Enhancer (CPFIS) is cataloged as a supported V1 product. The parser captures the published zero-charge single-premium, ad-hoc top-up, regular top-up, and nil-charge withdrawal path for the CPF-funded corridor through the open-ended no-MIP basis, plus the current ordinary death-benefit estimate as 105% of the single premium policy value and 100% of the top-up premium policy value.
Administrative charge is not applicable and switching is published as free, but switching behavior itself remains outside the current calculator surface.
This open-ended single-premium product uses the no-MIP basis; the review horizon is chosen in the policy seed rather than by product contract.
Open-ended products use a default 20-year review horizon in V1; adjust the horizon if you want a different analysis window.
Enter the one-time gross initial single premium lump sum in Policy Details if you want the upfront single-premium deduction to seed the starting policy value honestly.
Split single-premium and top-up policy-value history remains informational only beyond the modeled current ordinary death-benefit estimate.
Fund-level management fees and embedded custody or bank charges remain informational only because they are reflected through fund pricing rather than the policy charge surface.
Lapse, termination, and claim-side policy administration remain informational only.
